conflicts.about: Whether the service navigation keeps a Log out item, which Design Release 2.1 drops.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as authentication, overrides the prototype.
The DR2.1 service navigation has no Log out item.
The service navigation's Log out item links to /auth/sign-out.
The INS navigation's Log out link goes to /auth/sign-out.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling outranks the prototype: the prototype has no real sign-in, so it cannot express that a signed-in trader needs a way to sign out. Log out stays as the last navigation item in both frontends; everything else about the navigation follows DR2.1, including the new Templates item.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's rulings on the animals-frontend dashboard (status-driven card links, an always-sorted list) bind the DR2.1 dashboard now built in the INS frontend.

positions.says: inc-030 is rejected: the dashboard card keeps its status-driven links and is not flattened to Copy as new plus View.
inc-031 is rejected: the dashboard stays always sorted and no unsorted state is added.
A DR2.1 dashboard card's header has a Copy as new link and a View link only.
The DR2.1 list's Sort by select opens on 'Select one' ahead of Newest first, Oldest first and Arrival date.
The ruling limits DR1 to clashes with 'the real frontend' and does not say whether DR1 judgements apply to the INS frontend.

conflicts.outcome: Two readings build different dashboards: DR1 judged this exact difference, but on the animals-frontend dashboard, which DR1 itself says moves to the INS frontend. Raised as a question; the default follows the DR1 judgements, because the ruling says a DR1 judgement on the same difference wins.
conflicts.question: Do DR1's rulings inc-030 (status-driven card links) and inc-031 (always sorted, no 'Select one'), made on the animals-frontend dashboard, apply to the DR2.1 dashboard being built in the INS frontend?
conflicts.default: Yes. INS dashboard cards keep status-driven actions (a draft: Resume, Copy as new, Delete; a submitted notification: View, Amend, Copy as new, Delete; one being amended: Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete), and every list is always sorted, Newest first by default, with no 'Select one' option. Everything else on the card and the sort labels follows DR2.1.

conflicts.about: Which frontend holds the notifications dashboard and the address book.

positions.says: Rhys ruled on 2026-08-28 that the dashboard and the address book are temporary in the animals frontend and move to trade-imports-ins-frontend.
In DR2.1 the dashboard, templates and address book are all navigation targets inside the one prototype app.
The animals frontend has its own dashboard at /live-animals.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's ruling on where the dashboard and address book live ranks above the prototype, which is one app and cannot say which real service owns a page. The DR2.1 dashboard and address book are built in the INS frontend (which already owns the address book and an aggregated dashboard).

conflicts.about: What happens to the animals frontend's own dashboard, and where the journey's dashboard links go, once DR2.1's dashboard is in the INS frontend.

positions.says: The animals frontend's Dashboard navigation item links to its own dashboard at /live-animals.
The overview's 'Return to dashboard' button links to the animals frontend's dashboard.
Parity work against the animals-frontend dashboard buys nothing that travels, so its increments were blocked pending a fresh ruling.
The INS dashboard's 'Start a new notification' goes to the animals frontend's /live-animals dashboard, not straight into a journey.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 has one dashboard; the real service has two. Nothing settles whether the animals-frontend dashboard is retired or which one the journey links to, so it is a question with a default.
conflicts.question: Once the DR2.1 dashboard is built in the INS frontend, where do the live-animals journey's dashboard links go, and does the animals frontend's own dashboard at /live-animals stay?
conflicts.default: The journey's dashboard links (the service navigation's Dashboard, the overview's 'Return to dashboard', the confirmation page's 'Return to your dashboard', and the landing after a delete) go to the INS dashboard, and the INS 'Create new' starts a live-animals notification straight on its origin page. The animals frontend's /live-animals dashboard stays in place, unchanged, until a ruling retires it.

conflicts.about: Whether notification types other than live animals (germinal products, plants and the rest) come into this programme.

positions.says: DR2.1 starts every notification on a type page offering live animals, germinal products, plants for planting, potatoes and wood products.
The DR2.1 dashboard home has a Germinal products section beside Live animals.
The real journey is the Live Animals V4 data-field model.
Every INS dashboard row links into the live-animals journey; no other journey exists.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 designs five notification types but the goal names only the live-animals journey, and only live animals has a real journey. Building the other types would be new journeys, not a change to a real one, so it is a question with a default.
conflicts.question: DR2.1 offers five notification types and a germinal-products journey; does any type other than live animals come into this programme?
conflicts.default: No. Only live animals is built: 'Create new' starts the live-animals journey with no notification type page, the dashboard home shows only the Live animals section, templates are Live animals only, and the germinal-products fields, lists and dashboard and the plants section are out of scope.

conflicts.about: What is built for the dashboard states and counts no real service records today.

positions.says: DR2.1 fakes Action required, inspection, passed inspection and delayed states from a notification's position in the list.
A submitted notification is 'Submitted action required' when any conditional submission items are outstanding, otherwise 'Submitted'.
The dashboard home shows a Messages link with an unread count fixed at 12 and linking to '#'.
There are exactly four notification statuses; none for cancelled, rejected, in progress or a template.
The read model only sees DRAFT, SUBMITTED and DELETED statuses.

conflicts.outcome: Some DR2.1 states can be derived from the notification (outstanding items at submission); others (completion, delays, inspections, messages) come from border processes no real service records. Cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express, so a question with a default per state.
conflicts.question: DR2.1's dashboard shows Action required, Completed, Delayed, status changes, inspection and messages; what is built for each when no real service records most of them?
conflicts.default: Action required is built from the items outstanding at submission (no ITAHC document; required animal identifiers incomplete), recorded by the animals backend and carried to the INS read model. The Completed tab, the Status updates card and its changes page are built but stay empty (count 0) until a service records completion or status changes. Delayed, the inspection card and page, and the Messages link are not built.

conflicts.about: Whether the dashboard lists are limited to the signed-in organisation in this programme.

positions.says: The list is not scoped to the signed-in user or their organisation.
Organisation scoping of the list has been deferred to a later ticket.
The animals backend's dashboard list serves every trader's notifications to every caller.
Authentication and cross-service behaviour are real constraints that override the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1's dashboards show one trader's own notifications and live counts of them; the real read model shows everyone's, and scoping was deferred to a later ticket. Whether that ticket lands inside this programme is not settled by any source.
conflicts.question: Is organisation scoping of the dashboard lists, counts and searches built in this programme, though ins-backend deferred it to a later ticket?
conflicts.default: Yes. Every dashboard list, tab, count and search shows only the signed-in organisation's notifications; the INS read model records each notification's organisation from its events and the INS frontend sends the session's organisation.

conflicts.about: Whether saved addresses carry a type (what each address can be used for).

positions.says: A saved address is added with every ticked use as its address types.
Design release 1 gives every saved address one of seven types, Branch Address set apart.
inc-048 prescribes giving a saved address one or more roles and filtering each picker by its role; the address-book API must carry the type first.
Ruling cv-044: the address book is untyped and unroled, so a request that supplies a type is rejected.
Ruling cv-044: a request that supplies a role is rejected.
All five party pickers search the same untyped organisation address book, so any record can be any party.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 and DR1 (inc-048, inc-062) both type saved addresses, and both rank above the address-book service's ruling cv-044 and the frontend. An untyped record is a design choice, not a constraint the prototype cannot express. Addresses carry one or more uses; cv-044's refusal of a type or role is withdrawn.

conflicts.about: Where transporters an organisation adds are kept, so the journey list and the address book show the same records.

positions.says: A transporter added from the address book is saved to the address book as a transporter entry with its type, address, approval number and contact details.
The address book's Transporter tab lists transporters with Name, Address, Approval number and Type.
Transporters an organisation adds are held in the frontend process's memory, lost on restart, because there is no transporter register service yet.
The address record carries no transporter category or approval number field.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype keeps transporters in its session; the real service has no durable home for them. Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so where they live is a question with a default.
conflicts.question: Where are the transporters an organisation adds kept, so that the journey's transporter list and the address book's Transporter tab show the same records?
conflicts.default: In the address-book service, as transporter entries (type Commercial or Private, approval number, status New) owned by the organisation. The journey's transporter list reads them alongside the shipped transporters, the INS address book lists and adds them, and the animals frontend's in-memory store is retired.

conflicts.about: What answers DR2.1's UK and Northern Ireland address searches.

positions.says: The address search is a free-text type-ahead over organisation name, address and country.
The commercial transporter page offers an address search over Northern Ireland addresses.
The address lookup is a dev-only spike; how a real build would use one is still to be decided.
The spike's lookup client calls the INS backend's GET /address-lookup endpoint.
Locally the lookup answers from trade-imports-stub's simulator, which returns the same three London SW1A 1AA addresses for every search and no Northern Ireland address.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype searches a made-up list; the real service needs a real address source, which exists only as a spike. Locally that source is trade-imports-stub, which holds England addresses only and is not one of this programme's repos, so a Northern Ireland result cannot be shown on the local stack. Cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express.
conflicts.question: What real address source answers DR2.1's 'Search for an address' type-ahead in the address book, the journey's add-address pages and the commercial transporter page, and should trade-imports-stub gain Northern Ireland addresses so the commercial transporter search can return one locally?
conflicts.default: The INS backend's address lookup (the EUDPA-390 spike, made production-ready) answers every search, the chosen result fills the address fields, and 'Enter address manually' is always offered and is the no-JavaScript route. On the local workspace stack the lookup answers from trade-imports-stub unchanged: UK searches return its England addresses, and the commercial transporter search returns no address, so there it is shown only that no address outside Northern Ireland is offered and that manual entry works. In CDP environments the lookup answers from the real address gateway: UK searches return UK addresses and the commercial transporter search returns Northern Ireland addresses only. trade-imports-stub is not changed by this programme.

conflicts.about: Where the journey's own add-address page lives, given the animals frontend reads the address book and never writes it.

positions.says: Each selectable section has an add-address page inside the journey at <section path>/add-address.
The animals frontend only reads the address book; adding, changing and removing records belongs to the INS frontend, the only writer.
inc-053 leaves open whether the add-address route is a page in this frontend or a link out to the INS add page with a return URL.
In journey mode the INS add page keeps its heading and fields and changes only its cancel button.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 puts the page in the journey; the real service has one address-book writer (a cross-service constraint). The page cannot be built as written in the animals frontend without giving it a write path.
conflicts.question: Does DR2.1's journey add-address page live in the animals frontend, or in the INS frontend's add page reached through the existing handshake?
conflicts.default: In the INS frontend: the existing journey handshake opens the INS add page in journey mode, which shows DR2.1's journey add-address content (heading, section-specific search or manual entry, the other-uses question, 'Save and select' and 'Save and return to address page'), and returns to the animals journey with the address selected or not as the trader chose. The animals frontend stays read-only.

conflicts.about: Whether address forms ask for a County, which DR2.1 asks on some address pages and not others.

positions.says: The DR2.1 add-details step has no County field.
The DR2.1 edit page asks 'County (optional)'.
The journey's manual address entry has no County field.
county is optional and may be at most 100 characters.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 contradicts itself on County, so precedence cannot settle it; raised as a question with a default.
conflicts.question: DR2.1 asks for a County on its edit and permanent-address forms but not on its add forms; does every address form ask for 'County (optional)'?
conflicts.default: Yes. Every address form (add, edit, journey add-address, permanent address, transporter) keeps 'County (optional)', and the view page shows it only when it has a value, as DR2.1's view page does.

conflicts.about: Whether the arrival date is labelled 'at port of entry' or 'at destination'.

positions.says: The arrival details page asks for the 'Arrival date at port of entry'.
The review's Arrival details card labels the same value 'Arrival date at destination'.
Undecided whether the arrival date collected is arrival at the port of entry or at the place of destination; nothing changes until that ruling.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 contradicts itself, and DR1 left the same contradiction undecided (inc-145). A port of entry and a place of destination are different places, so only one label can be right.
conflicts.question: Is the arrival date the trader gives the arrival at the port of entry or at the place of destination?
conflicts.default: The port of entry: 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the question page, the review card and the validation messages, and 'Arrival date' on the dashboard card.

conflicts.about: Whether the country, port of entry and port of exit lists take DR2.1's contents.

positions.says: Rhys ruled that countries, regions, territories and ports are master reference data the service will take from MDM.
A finding whose fix is the content of a master reference-data list is deferred rather than built.
The DR2.1 country list is the 27 EU member states.
The DR2.1 country list also offers 11 territories shown as 'Name (Parent)'.
The DR2.1 country list also offers the three crown dependencies.
The DR2.1 port of exit list holds ten exit border control posts.
The DR2.1 port of entry list holds 205 airports and sea ports.
ADR 0002: countries are a managed domain, sourced from MDM.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's MDM ruling is a judgement on this same kind of difference and ranks above the prototype. List contents come from MDM through reference-data; DR2.1's list contents are not copied, and the port of exit keeps the port of entry list until MDM carries an approved-for-animals attribute. How the lists are presented follows DR2.1.

conflicts.about: Which pages end with the three save controls, and whether user-facing controls may say 'hub'.

positions.says: Rule (b): only the pages the overview links to end with the three controls; a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone.
The secondary button reads 'Save and return to overview', never 'hub', because the page it leads to is headed 'Overview'.
Design release 1's extra cancel destinations ('Cancel and return to dashboard' on the transporter forms) were not adopted.
Design release 1's per-page 'Continue' labels on the transporter-add pages were left out rather than ported.
A DR2.1 picker ends with 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
The DR2.1 CPH page offers 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
The DR2.1 origin page shows a single 'Save and continue' button.
Both DR2.1 transporter add pages have a 'Cancel and return to dashboard' button.
The DR2.1 transporter type page has a 'Continue' button.
The DR2.1 contact address page reads 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
The DR2.1 per-animal permanent address page offers 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 judged these same differences (rule (b) by Sam on 2026-08-21, the 'overview' rename, the rejected per-page button pattern) and ranks above the prototype. Pages the overview links to end with the three controls; pages reached from another page (pickers, CPH, transporter type and add pages, permanent address) end with the primary 'Save and continue' alone; no control says 'hub' or 'Cancel and return to dashboard'.

conflicts.about: Whether the real services keep validation rules DR2.1 does not have.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation, overrides the prototype.
No error message is shown for a missing, badly formed or out-of-range arrival date.
The CPH number page has no validation.
A live-animal identifier with no length limit is never rejected for its content.
The address edit page sets no format rule for email, phone or postcode and no maximum lengths.
The address book add-details step has no format rules and no length limits.
The arrival date must fall between 7 days before today and 6 months after today.
email must be in a valid email format.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling names validation as a real constraint that overrides the prototype. The real services keep their validation (arrival date window and real-date checks, list membership for countries and ports, CPH digit and length checks, 58-character identifier and reference limits, address field lengths and email format, document file checks). Where DR2.1 has a message for the same rule, DR2.1's wording is used.

conflicts.about: What 'Copy as new' carries into the new draft.

positions.says: Copy as new carries over the origin details including the internal reference.
Copy as new carries over the selected species and commodity selections.
Copy as new carries over the import reason and every follow-up, the exit date included.
Copy as new carries over certification purpose and unweaned animals.
Copy clears the origin's internal reference.
Copy clears every complement's numbers and species list.
Copy clears the unweaned animals answer.
Copy clears the exit date.

conflicts.outcome: What a copy keeps is a product rule, not a persistence constraint; the prototype ranks above the backend. A copy keeps the internal reference, the species chosen (with their numbers cleared), unweaned animals and the exit date, as DR2.1 does.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Health certificate' is offered as a document type.

positions.says: After ITAHC, the DR2.1 document types are Veterinary health certificate through Other, thirteen in all, with no Health certificate.
Existing ruling (EUDPA-310): every GBN-AG document type is selectable; Design release 1 held Health certificate back and EUDPA-310 offers it again.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype ranks above the frontend's ruling, and offering fewer types breaks no codelist: every offered type still has its GBN-AG code. The select offers DR2.1's thirteen types; a document already saved as Health certificate keeps its type.

conflicts.about: The accompanying-document size limit, which the hosting platform caps.

positions.says: The attachment hint says files must be smaller than 50MB.
The limit is 10MB to stay inside CDP's 10 MiB ingress cap; it was put back from 50 until the ingress cap is raised.
The CDP ingress request-body cap must be confirmed as at least 50,001,024 bytes before 50MB is deployed; nothing confirms it.
The backend accepts files up to 52428800 bytes (50 MB).

conflicts.outcome: The platform ingress is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and whether it allows 50MB is unconfirmed. A 50MB hint before the cap is raised would give traders a platform error page instead of a validation message.
conflicts.question: Has the CDP ingress request-body cap in front of the animals frontend been raised to at least 50MB (EUDPA-518), so the document limit can follow DR2.1?
conflicts.default: The limit stays 10MB, with its hint and error, until the ingress cap is confirmed; it then becomes 50MB with DR2.1's '50MB' wording, in every environment at once.

conflicts.about: Whether features the real services have and DR2.1 does not show are removed.

positions.says: The ruling does not say whether a feature a real service has that DR2.1 does not show counts as a difference to remove.
An answered party row offers an 'Edit details' link that edits the notification's copy only.
A document row offers a 'View file' link once its scan has completed clean.
A recoverable backend failure shows a 'There is a problem' banner and keeps the trader's answers.

conflicts.outcome: A gap in the ruling that decides a lot of work: many real features (no-JavaScript routes, error states, virus results, party edits) have no DR2.1 counterpart.
conflicts.question: Where a real service has a feature DR2.1 does not show at all, is it removed?
conflicts.default: No. It is kept, unless DR2.1 shows a different way to do the same job, in which case DR2.1's way replaces it and the real feature stays only as the no-JavaScript route where one is needed. Copy that DR2.1 leaves out of a page is removed.

conflicts.about: When an animal counts as identified: one identifier filled, or every identifier for its commodity.

positions.says: An animal's identification entry counts as complete only when every identifier field for its species has a value.
Every animal-identifier record must carry at least one identifier, following V4.
Whether DR1's every-identifier rule or V4's at-least-one rule governs inc-103 is undecided; only the design authority can say.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 deferred this without a judgement, so the ruling's default applies: the prototype wins over the frontend. An animal counts as identified only when every identifier its commodity asks for has a value; the identifier sets were already corrected (no tattoo on cattle), so the ordering constraint DR1 recorded is met.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's blocked and deferred rows stop DR2.1 differences from being built.

positions.says: Where DR1 already made a judgement on that same difference, it is followed.
Only a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint, overrides the prototype.
Twelve address increments are blocked as deferred until the team's address work settles, and none may be built without a fresh ruling.
Nineteen dashboard and address-book-scoping increments are blocked as deferred decisions, and none may be built without a fresh ruling.
None of the eight blocked address rows records a decision on the Design release 1 difference itself.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling outranks the DR1 notes and is the fresh ruling those blocks wait for. The blocks and deferrals were holds for collision or dependency during DR1 parity, not judgements on the differences, so DR2.1 is built for them (permanent address page, party page layout and copy actions, role-scoped pickers, contact branch addresses, live region prefix, outstanding identifier bullet). DR1's actual judgements (rejections, rule (b), the MDM ruling) still stand.

conflicts.about: Whether the live-animal commodity and species list takes DR2.1's contents.

positions.says: The DR2.1 live-animal commodity list is the UK chapter 01 commodities with their IPAFFS species, sorted by name.
DR2.1 names the cattle commodity 'Cattle', code 0102, with eleven species.
The commodity picker offers five commodities today: Cow, Horse, Cat, Dog and Fish.
Commodity, species and allow-list data is stub data held in the frontend and does not prove compatibility with master data.
A finding whose fix is the content of a master reference-data list is deferred, because editing a hard-coded list is work MDM replaces.
The MDM ruling does not cover the per-commodity identifier findings: their fix is local.

conflicts.outcome: Commodities and species come from MDM in production, but DR1's MDM ruling names only countries, regions, territories and ports, and DR1 warns against sweeping work into the MDM block on the word 'list'. Two readings build different catalogues.
conflicts.question: Does the live-animals commodity and species list take DR2.1's contents (19 commodities, names such as 'Cattle'), or wait for master data through reference-data?
conflicts.default: The list's contents (which commodities and species, and how each is named) wait for master data, as DR1 ruled for master reference lists, so in every environment the list stays today's five commodities (cattle, horses, cats, dogs, fish). DR2.1's per-commodity rules by commodity code (identifiers, packaging, unweaned, CPH, permanent address) and its common-name display apply now to those five, and are proved for them. The rules for pigs (0103), sheep (010410), goats (010420) and ferrets are not built or tested in this programme in any environment, because no environment offers those commodities; they are built when master data supplies them.

conflicts.about: Where the phase banner's feedback link goes.

positions.says: RULING: the phase banner's feedback link is mailto:APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk, and no /feedback route or survey URL may be invented.
The DR2.1 phase banner's feedback link points at '#'.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 judged this same difference (a placeholder link) and ranks above the prototype. The feedback link stays the APHA service desk mailto.

conflicts.about: Where templates are stored and which frontend serves the template pages.

positions.says: Templates are held only in the user's session, not shared between users or kept beyond the session.
Templates have no owner, sharing or organisation scope.
There is no notification status for a template.
Persistence, authentication and cross-service behaviour are real constraints that override the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: Templates are new everywhere. The prototype keeps them in a session with no owner; a real service must store and scope them, and nothing settles which service or frontend owns them.
conflicts.question: Where are templates stored, who can see them, and which frontend serves the template pages?
conflicts.default: The animals backend stores templates as records separate from notifications, owned by the signed-in organisation. The Manage templates, template name, view and delete pages and the template-mode journey live in the animals frontend, and the Templates navigation item and the dashboard's 'Use template' button in both frontends link to Manage templates.
